name: manual_4121f3
claim: When merging tracked memory across branches, never hand-edit a graduated candidate claim: its id must remain a tooling derivation of that exact claim, so sanitizing or rewording the claim silently invalidates the id and the memory-records gate rejects the commit. Union the JSONL files by id while leaving the target branch rows byte-intact, append only genuinely new rows, then re-render the derived markdown; if a row genuinely needs new text, re-mint it through the memory tooling instead of editing it in place.

decisions.notes: Bringing a session memory commit onto another branch conflicted in lessons.jsonl, the episodic log, the rendered LESSONS.md and the working file. A union that deduplicated naively also dropped legitimate intra-file duplicates from the target branch, which had to be re-done as append-only. Then the commit was rejected by the memory-records gate because two graduated candidate JSONs had been carried over with sanitized claim text, so their ids no longer matched the tooling derivation; restoring those two files to the branch versions and re-rendering resolved it and all four gates passed.
